units.translation: I will stand as an enemy with an enemy.
And I stood speechless with fear.
Let us stand out of the way.
Stand upon the decks of the towers.
Come, saviors of the city, and stand in good seats.
And upon the body – having stood.
Having stood near the altar of Zeus Ktesios.
before I make you master of your children
Let us first inquire into this disease.
But if some ray of the sun sees him pale and seeing
You inquire well about your father.

because οἶστρος [gadfly] is written in some manuscripts of Hephaestion and Priscian. The scholiast on Apollonius Rhodius 4, 284 says that the Ister flows down from the Hyperboreans and the Rhipaean mountains. He said this following Aeschylus in the Prometheus Unbound, who says this (fr. 197).
The Ister gives birth to such maidens.

Thus corrected from the apograph. In M is ἰσχναίει [makes lean], with v written over ει.
And having made you lean while alive, I will take you below.
And from these he drank beer, making himself lean over time.
And do not make your swelling spirit lean by force.
of hard and firm earth, which is often called σκληρά [hard]
But the strength of god is still superior.
For all the Asian-born strength has gone.
the strength of the spear-headed lance
For the royal strength has utterly perished.
the strength of the traveling torch
When shall we show the strength of our mouths?
For where strength and justice are yoked together
to be in no way less strong than Zeus
For no oath is stronger than Zeus.
Hold back, lest I be overcome by fear.
Perhaps I seem to you to be saying ancient things.
For perhaps some herald or envoy might come.
